sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports and router setup
sections.what: Loads the web tools and the three functions from the defaults module, then creates the router.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the route code thin and the data logic in the defaults module.
sections.watch_out: The three function names must match the defaults module exactly, or the app will fail to start.

sections.name: EnhancedDefaultsRequest
sections.title: Request shape for enhanced defaults
sections.what: Describes the enhanced defaults request: a required industry, an optional company name, and periods defaulting to 5.
sections.why: Likely reason: the shape the enhanced route checks before it runs.
sections.watch_out: Unlike the GET route, periods here has no minimum or maximum.

sections.name: list_industries
sections.title: Listing supported industries
sections.what: Returns the supported industries with their descriptions and examples.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the frontend build an industry picker.
sections.watch_out: The list comes from the defaults module, so an industry added there appears here automatically.

sections.name: get_defaults_for_industry
sections.title: Defaults for one industry
sections.what: Returns default assumptions for one industry over a set number of periods, with periods limited to 1 to 20.
sections.why: Likely reason: the simple lookup route the screens use before any AI refinement.
sections.watch_out: How an unknown industry name is handled is decided in the defaults module and is not visible here.

sections.name: get_enhanced_defaults
sections.title: AI-enhanced defaults
sections.what: Passes the industry, company name and periods to the AI-enhanced defaults function and returns what it produces.
sections.why: Likely reason: a planned step to adjust defaults using company research. The docstring describes this as future behavior.
sections.watch_out: If no AI provider is available, the result may fall back to plain defaults or fail. This file does not show which.

summary: Provides routes that return default financial assumptions for an industry, plus a route meant to add AI-refined values.
purpose: Let the user start a model with sensible starting numbers for their industry instead of typing everything in.
why: Likely reason: saves time and gives a reasonable starting point for each industry.
how: One route lists the supported industries. Another returns defaults for one industry over a chosen number of periods. A third sends the industry and company name to the AI-enhanced function. Periods are limited to 1 to 20 only on the GET route.
inputs: An industry name in the web address or request body, an optional company name, and the number of periods (default 5).
outputs: A success status with the industry and periods used, and a defaults dictionary whose structure comes from the defaults module.
risks: The enhanced route has no range check on periods, so very large numbers are accepted. An industry name containing a slash will not match the route.
debug: If the defaults look wrong, check the defaults module, not this file. If the enhanced route fails, check what get_ai_enhanced_defaults does with the company name and whether an AI provider is set up.
